glance_takeaway: The page explains how diffusion image generators (Stable Diffusion, DALL-E 3, Flux) work: a fixed process gradually destroys images into noise over ~1000 steps, and a network learns to reverse it one small step at a time; generation applies that learned step repeatedly starting from fresh random noise, so no photo is edited and no database is consulted. Training means guessing the noise that was added to an image at a random level, repeated billions of times, with mean-squared error driving weight updates. Nearly every variant exists to make sampling cheaper, shrinking ~1000 steps down to as few as 1-4, which a 'variant zoo' section below apparently catalogs.

render_issues: none — all six Mermaid flowcharts rendered correctly in the screenshot; note the page depends on a CDN-loaded mermaid.js at view time, so offline it would degrade to raw diagram source.
strengths: Exceptional factual coverage and precision: all 15 ground-truth facts land, most with the exact representative numbers (786,432 -> 16,384, ~48x, s = 7.5, s > 12-15, 10-20% prompt dropout, NFE).

The variant zoo diagram directly encodes the step-count ladder (~1000 -> 20-50 -> 10-20 -> 1-4) with a sampler-vs-retrain color distinction, which is the single most important comparative structure in the material.
Honest caveats throughout: memorization exception, img2img exception, compression-bottleneck quality ceiling, high-guidance artifact regime, diminishing returns above ~50 steps.
Clear six-section structure in a sensible pedagogical order (mechanism -> training -> variants -> latent -> guidance -> misconceptions), easy to relocate any topic.
weaknesses: The diagrams are thin as visual encodings — most of the actual content lives in long, parenthetical-dense caption paragraphs in small muted text; the flowcharts are essentially sentences with arrows, so the visual channel carries less than it appears to.

Color semantics are inconsistent across diagrams (blue = 'learned' in some, 'same network + smarter sampler' in the zoo; green = 'output' in some, 'retrained objective' in the zoo) and the legend is buried in one caption, which can quietly mislead.
The core-mechanism diagram's dotted edge from 'Pure noise' to 'Fresh random noise' labeled 'training: a network learns to undo one small step' is topologically confusing on first read.
Above the fold, latent diffusion and guidance (T3, T4) are entirely invisible; the glance conveys only the core mechanism and the fewer-steps motive.
The sequential-evaluation bottleneck (why 1000 steps cannot be parallelized) and the SDE / probability-flow-ODE framing are omitted rather than simplified.
evaluator_notes: Accuracy is mechanically 10.0 (15/15 conveyed, 0 distorted, 0 contradicted) — this page is unusually faithful to the ground truth, with nearly every representative number present verbatim; the notes on F5/F8/F13 record partial omissions within otherwise-conveyed facts. The overall is held below the accuracy by the glance pass (only T1 and the headline of T2 land above the fold) and by visual craft: the Mermaid format pushes the real explanatory load into dense captions, and reused colors mean different things in different diagrams. Overall = 0.35*10.0 + 0.30*6.0 + 0.15*7.5 + 0.10*7.5 + 0.10*6.0 = 7.775 -> 7.8.
